issues.legal_issue: A civil court retains jurisdiction to decide a disputed landlord-tenant relationship when the special statutory forum is assigned only specified disputes between landlords and tenants.
material_facts: The suit sought an injunction against entry onto land, and the claimant asserted ownership and personal cultivation.
The opposing parties admitted the claimant’s title but asserted that they were tenants in possession of separate portions of the land.
The statutory provision assigned the Collector five specified categories of disputes between a tenant and a landlord, but did not expressly assign disputes over whether that relationship existed.
The civil court had to decide whether the opposing parties were tenants before it could determine the suit.
issues.conclusion: The dispute over the existence of the landlord-tenant relationship was within the civil court’s jurisdiction and was not assigned to the Collector under section 7(1).
issues.legal_principle: Exclusion of civil-court jurisdiction is not readily inferred and must be express or clearly implied (Secretary of State v. Mask & Co.). Section 7(1) specifies five categories of disputes and presupposes that the parties are landlord and tenant; it does not cover a dispute about that status. The provisions governing the Collector’s inquiry and appeal, including sections 7(2), 7(3), 7(6), 7(7) and 11, support that construction. The Act’s relationship to the Orissa Tenancy Act, 1913, under section 13, and that Act’s provisions for formal inquiries and appeals (sections 192 and 204) and for civil suits concerning whether the relationship exists (section 126(3)(c)) also support it.

predicates.civil_suit_about_land_possession: A party brought a civil suit concerning possession of land.
predicates.landlord_tenant_status_contested: The parties disputed whether a landlord-tenant relationship existed between them.
predicates.special_forum_authority_confined_to_enum: The law assigned a special forum authority over specified disputes between landlords and tenants, without assigning it authority to determine whether that relationship existed.

issues.definition: When a civil suit concerning land requires resolution of a disputed landlord-tenant status and the special forum’s authority is confined to specified tenant disputes, the civil court may determine that status.

issues.legal_issue: Disputes between an established landlord and tenant that are outside the categories assigned to the Collector are within the revenue court’s jurisdiction rather than the civil court’s jurisdiction.
material_facts: The Act provided that, subject to the disputes assigned to the Collector, disputes arising between a landlord and tenant were cognisable by the revenue court and not by the civil court.
The court construed that provision together with the provision directing that the Act be read as part of the applicable tenancy legislation.
The court explained that the revenue court’s jurisdiction over these disputes was subject to the relevant provisions of the parent tenancy legislation.
issues.conclusion: Subject to the disputes covered by section 7(1), section 8(1) assigns disputes arising between landlord and tenant to the revenue court, not the civil court.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 8(1) and 13, read together, provide that disputes between landlord and tenant other than those covered by section 7(1) are cognisable by the revenue court, with the relevant provisions of the Orissa Tenancy Act, 1913 applying to their trial.

predicates.landlord_tenant_dispute_proceeding: A proceeding concerns a dispute between a landlord and a tenant.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_established: The parties’ landlord-tenant relationship has been admitted or established.
predicates.dispute_outside_specified_collector_cate: The dispute does not fall within the categories assigned to the Collector.
predicates.law_assigns_other_tenant_disputes_to_rev: The law assigns tenant-landlord disputes outside the specified categories to a revenue forum instead of a civil court.

issues.definition: When an established landlord and tenant have a dispute outside the specified categories and the law assigns other such disputes to a revenue forum, that forum has exclusive jurisdiction.
